details.description: API key and secrets are hard-coded in the source file enabling accidental exposure (THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY, DB_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET).
details.fix_explanation: Removed hard-coded secrets and switched to reading configuration values from environment variables. Use secure secret management for production (vaults/CI secrets).
details.secure_code_snippet:
THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY = os.environ.get("THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY")
DB_PASSWORD = os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD")
JWT_SECRET = os.environ.get("JWT_SECRET")

details.description: User-supplied input is embedded directly into the SQL query string, allowing SQL injection.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized SQL queries (placeholders) and validate/limit input length to avoid injection attacks.
details.secure_code_snippet:
query = "SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name = ? LIMIT 100"
cursor.execute(query, (username,))

details.vulnerability_type: OS command injection (shelling out with untrusted data)
details.description: The code calls os.system with a formatted string that contains user input, enabling command injection.
details.fix_explanation: Do not call the shell with user-controlled strings. Use Python's tarfile module or subprocess with argument lists and validate file paths to prevent path traversal.
details.secure_code_snippet:
with tarfile.open(archive_path, "w:gz") as tar:
    tar.add(target_resolved, arcname=target_resolved.name)

details.description: Falling back to eval() on JSON parse error allows arbitrary code execution from attacker-controlled input.
details.fix_explanation: Do not use eval. Use json.loads only, with a safe fallback to ast.literal_eval if necessary, and reject or error on unsafe input.

details.vulnerability_type: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) / Unsafe request handling
details.description: requests.get() is called on user-supplied URLs without validation, timeouts, or protection from private/internal addresses.
details.fix_explanation: Validate the URL (scheme only http/https), resolve hostnames and reject calls to private/loopback/reserved IPs. Add a timeout and verify SSL certificates.
details.secure_code_snippet:
if not _is_safe_url(url):
    raise ValueError("disallowed url")
res = requests.get(url, timeout=5.0)
res.raise_for_status()

details.vulnerability_type: Insufficient input validation and unsafe request.json usage
details.description: The original code used request.json[...] without checking for presence or types, which may throw exceptions or allow malformed payloads.
details.fix_explanation: Use request.get_json(silent=True) or request.get_json(force=False) and validate payload keys and types; return 400 errors on missing or invalid data.
details.secure_code_snippet:
payload = request.get_json(silent=True)
if not payload or 'url' not in payload: ...

details.description: The original code printed the fully formed SQL query (including user input) to stdout which may leak sensitive data to logs.
details.fix_explanation: Avoid printing sensitive content. Use structured logging at appropriate levels and redact or avoid logging secrets/PII.
details.secure_code_snippet: logger.debug("Executing DB query with parameterized input")

details.description: app.run(debug=True) enables the Flask debugger and interactive console — dangerous in production.
details.fix_explanation: Control debug mode via an environment variable; default to disabled. Never hard-code debug=True in source.
